exposure: intake of protein from plant sources
intake of protein from animal sources
outcome: development of pharmacologically treated hypertension (defined as antihypertensive medication usage >90 days after delivery)
cohort: The study included 59,967 Norwegian mothers from the Norwegian Mother, Father and Child Cohort Study (MoBa) recruited between 2004-2008, who did not have hypertension before pregnancy.
finding: Intake of protein from dairy sources, particularly milk/yoghurt, was inversely associated with hypertension, while protein from red meat was positively associated with developing hypertension up to ten years after pregnancy.
